title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwritten text is on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7 Exposé IX (§10.2, the monodromy pairing). It belongs to Grothendieck's preparation for his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The goal is a Sullivan-type theory of 'polynomial forms' on simplicial sets over an arbitrary base ring k. Divided powers replace rational coefficients so that a Poincaré lemma can hold integrally.

Setting.
- For each n there is a bigraded algebra C^{**}_n. It is presumably the divided-power polynomial de Rham complex of the algebraic n-simplex Δ_n over k.
- These form a simplicial object n ↦ C^{**}_n.
- For a simplicial set 𝒳 one sets C^{**}(𝒳) = Γ(𝒳, C^{**}) = Hom(𝒳, C^{**}_•).
- H^{**}(𝒳) is its cohomology. T_∞(H^{**}(𝒳)) is some associated graded-commutative ('alternée') algebra, containing among other things M_∞. The meaning of T_∞ and M_∞ is unclear from this page.

Axiom wanted. H^{**}(𝒳) should lie in the essential image of extension of scalars from k-modules. That is, it should be written, essentially uniquely, as H^{**}_c(𝒳) = H^*(X) ⊗_k S_k. Here S_k is a fixed bigraded coefficient algebra, the 'cohomology of a point' for this theory. Ordinary cohomology H^*(X) should then be recovered inside the graded-algebra structure of T_∞(H^{**}(𝒳)).

Specialisation. Taking 𝒳 = Δ_n, the axiom forces each C^{**}_n to be a resolution of S_k. This is the Poincaré lemma for the PD forms on the simplex. Grothendieck then rephrases his requirement as a condition for all 𝒳.

Sheaf-theoretic reformulation.
- View n ↦ C^{**}_n as a sheaf of complexes ('structure de type D') on the topos of (semi-)simplicial sets.
- The cosimplicial degree is treated as the principal degree.
- There is an augmentation from the constant sheaf, S_k → C^{**}_n, which is a quasi-isomorphism in D(graded S_k-modules).
- This gives the diagram (1): RΓ(𝒳, S_k) → RΓ(𝒳, C^{**}) ← C^{**}(𝒳) = Γ(𝒳, C^{**}).
- The right arrow should be an isomorphism because each C^{**}_n is Γ-acyclic, an 'extendability' property.
- The resulting map is a comparison morphism of divided-power algebras.

This is the standard Cartan / Sullivan / Bousfield–Gugenheim de Rham-theorem argument, transposed to the topos of simplicial sets with PD coefficients.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is a sketch: the acyclicity of C^{**}_n (Poincaré lemma) and the Γ-acyclicity needed for the right arrow of (1) are stated as requirements, not proved.
The exact meaning of T_∞, M_∞ and S_k cannot be determined from this page alone, so the precise form of the axiom H^{**} = H^* ⊗_k S_k is uncertain.

ideas.what: Simplicial polynomial (divided-power) de Rham forms C^{**}_n on Δ_n, with cochain algebra C^{**}(𝒳) = Γ(𝒳, C^{**}) for simplicial sets 𝒳 over an arbitrary ring k
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan polynomial forms A_PL; integral / PD versions (Cenkl–Porter forms, divided-power de Rham)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976), H. Cartan (1976); integral versions Cenkl–Porter (c. 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the 1976 IHÉS talk (unpublished); unsure about any circulated notes

ideas.what: Axiom that the theory's cohomology is extended from ordinary cohomology: H^{**}(𝒳) ≅ H^*(X) ⊗_k S_k, with S_k the cohomology of a point
ideas.modern_name: Coefficient algebra / base-change form of a multiplicative cohomology theory; Künneth-type rigidity

ideas.what: Viewing C^{**}_• as a sheaf on the topos of simplicial sets, resolving the constant sheaf S_k, to obtain RΓ(𝒳, S_k) → RΓ(𝒳, C^{**}) ← Γ(𝒳, C^{**})
ideas.modern_name: Extendable (Γ-acyclic) simplicial coefficient systems; abstract de Rham theorem via Poincaré lemma

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic integral/PD analogue of Sullivan's de Rham theorem. The coefficients are a fixed bigraded algebra S_k, and cohomology is required to be of the form H^*(X) ⊗ S_k. This is a programme for commutative cochain models over arbitrary rings, a problem later attacked by others with different tools.
missed.quote: H^{**}_c(𝒳) = H^*_c(X) ⊗_k S_k ... On peut considérer C^{**}_n comme un faisceau (: structure de type D) sur le topos ... augmentation par le faisceau constant S_k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links to integral and p-adic homotopy theory. Relevant later work includes Cenkl–Porter integral forms, Mandell's E∞ cochains, and recent work on derived/PD commutative cochain models. Grothendieck's 1976 approach could document an early attempt at commutative integral cochain algebras with divided powers.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early, unpublished sketch of an integral/divided-power Sullivan-type cochain theory in topos language. It is historically interesting but fragmentary, and the argument shown is the standard Poincaré-lemma / extendability one.
transcription_corrections: 'T_∞' appears as a tau-like symbol 'τ_∞' (or T with subscript ∞) applied to H^{**}(𝒳).
'[Il ... sait que' is likely 'Il se fait que' or 'On sait que'.
'topos (SS[?]' is likely the topos of semi-simplicial sets, 'SS'.
The last line reads 'C^{**}(𝒳) = Γ(𝒳, C^{**})', with the closing parenthesis cut off.
